messages.author: 0e8054b18ece3e51
messages.subject: Time Varying Parameter Model
parts:
Dear all,

I am relatively new to INLA, coming from Stan/JAGS. I am trying to estimate a time varying parameter model, but I have difficulty finding examples online.
My data consist of real estate transaction prices. Data like this is an extremely unbalanced panel. I.e. we have many properties, but they only get sold every so often. To track price changes over time one could (in a initial step) allow coefficients to be time-varying, so;

prices_it = beta_t*X_it + epsilon_it

Where subscript i are the individual properties (i = 1,...,N), t is the time of sale of that property (which is an index running from t=1,...,T), X are the characteristics and epsilon are the residuals, which we (for now) assume to be Gaussian. The coefficient beta_t is assumed to follow a random walk. However (and I do not have to explain this to you...), whenever I specify a variable to follow a random walk, it does so OVER the variable. Consider the example below;

formula = price ~ f(nrUnits, model = "rw1", values = as.factor(seq(minSize,maxSize))) 

This will give me the value over the number of units (nrUnits), not how the coefficient changed over time. I was thinking of trying something like interactions between a period index and the variables. So something like this;

formula =  price ~  f(periodIndex, model = "rw1", values = as.factor(seq(minPeriod,maxPeriod))):nrUnits 

And do this for all variables. I am not sure if this would work (and it `looks' kinda ugly), but if you have any suggestions, that would be much appreciated!
Alex

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Time Varying Parameter Model
parts:
f(time,x, model="rw1", constr=FALSE)

will give you a RW1, Z(time), say, with 'weights' x(time), so the
contribution to the linear predictor is

Z(time) * x(time)

this would be a generalization of \beta * x, where 'beta' is allowed to
vary over time.

let me know...

H
